evidence: createApp wires Express routes (app.get/app.post) and hands every business operation to OrderService methods (placeOrder, advance, cancel, addProduct, stockLevel, listOrders).
view(o: Order) turns the domain object into a response shape and formats placedAt with toISOString(), which is presentation/transport work.
The STATUS table and the error middleware map DomainError codes and SyntaxError to HTTP status codes, which is a transport concern.
ACTIONS maps route names to OrderState values but does not check whether a transition is valid; service.advance does that.
The `items must be an array` check in POST /orders only validates the shape of the request payload.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts is an Express HTTP adapter, and everything it does is transport work that belongs in infrastructure. It sets up routes, reads values out of request bodies, params and query strings, turns domain objects into JSON views, and maps error codes to HTTP status codes. The ACTIONS table only links URL action names to target states. Deciding whether a transition is allowed is left to service.advance, which belongs to the application or domain layer. The check that `items` is an array is a shape check on the request payload, not a business rule. Placing orders, checking stock and other business decisions are handed to OrderService. I found nothing about persistence, and no business rules in this file.
